I enrolled my son at Goonj Music School for guitar classes. Kshitij, the owner and main teacher, is genuinely talented and knows music well, but he is extremely loud and keeps shouting most of the time. What disappointed me more were some of the other teachers. Instead of properly teaching the children, they would often sit and loudly play their own instruments. Because the shop is small, it becomes chaotic and difficult for the kids to focus or learn anything properly. A few of them also came across as rude and unprofessional.

One thing that made me especially uncomfortable was hearing some of the young teachers pass comments about children’s mothers in front of other kids. I found that very inappropriate for a place where parents trust teachers with their children.

The school has potential, but overall the atmosphere was not what I expected for young kids learning music.

featured_reviews.name: Lubaina Sadriwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
A very real review from the world’s most distracted student:
So, after spending my entire childhood wanting to learn the guitar, I finally; 32 years and one kid later, decided to pursue this dream. Now, I have severe ADHD, which basically means I have the attention span of a hyperactive squirrel. I can lose motivation faster than it takes to tune a string (which is saying a lot).
So yeah, I’m pretty much every teacher’s nightmare student.
But Robin Sir at Improvise Music Academy didn’t even flinch. Just when I thought he’d finally throw me out for forgetting chords for the tenth time, he showed next-level patience. He even went so far as to alphabetically number the strings for me, like, who does that? A saint disguised as a music teacher, that’s who.
I actually used to look forward to his classes (and trust me, that’s rare). He’s humble, genuinely interested in every student’s progress, and has this uncanny ability to adapt his teaching style to each person’s learning speed, which explains why the name Improvise fits so perfectly.
Robin Sir doesn’t just teach music, he lives it. He’s incredibly talented, deeply passionate, and somehow manages to teach both little kids and distracted adults (me) with the same calm energy of a monk.
So if you’re looking to learn guitar, or any instrument, really this is the place to go. I still have a long way to go with my guitar, but I’m actually excited about it. And who knows, maybe one day I’ll even start the piano too (pray for Robin Sir 😅).

featured_reviews.name: Nithya Prince
featured_reviews.review_text: I am taking Piano classes here from September 2021. Learning Piano was always a dream and a thing I kept trying for a long time, unfortunately I didn’t get to learn in my childhood days. So at 27, working from home during covid, I joined this class. The curriculum used here is very easy to learn. Every concept is covered well. You can choose to have the classes as per your interest in taking exams like Trinity or ABRSM Board as well. I also got to learn my favourite songs in piano and keyboard style. Anita mam is a good teacher and checks the homework videos I send her and gives me regular feedback. And all this has been virtually which is impossible to believe, I am confident than before of learning this skill and I am very much happy on the progress I am making.
